summary: @servicetitan/restrict-imports preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package's preinstall script runs setup.mjs, which downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases and then invokes a bundled 727KB sibling file math_init.js under that runtime via execFileSync. math_init.js is heavily obfuscated Bun-compiled JavaScript (hex-numeric constant table, string-array rotator, renamed identifiers, no readable strings) and is not referenced from dist/index.js or any documented code path of the webpack import-restriction plugin. The published scope @servicetitan/* and the small legitimate plugin in dist/ do not require a second language runtime; the payload ships alongside the legitimate code and executes automatically on npm install. Fetching Bun's official runtime is by itself aggressive-but-legitimate, but here it is used solely to run an obfuscated in-tarball payload that has no relation to the declared plugin functionality, matching the alternate-runtime-dropper shape used to bypass Node-based scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
